touches.text: A shim waking its device never takes more than 60 s. A sync caller waits at most 60 s for the wake, then gets "not now" back; a wake that misses 60 s is a trouble. 600 s is the limit for an inference call to come back, not for a wake.
A message is addressed to a name (a device instance), never to a connection. A shim that restarts reconnects and answers to the same name, so restarting it never restarts the bus.
Messages sit in a SMALL buffer in memory. WHY: in memory is faster.

A message nobody picks up within n milliseconds is pushed out of the buffer to the database, into a table that is just a table of messages. That table is the bus's exception to the memory model (4.3.1.5): it is not learning, and the buffer in front of it is what keeps the bus fast.
Two kinds of request: Send, asynchronous, like sending an email; and Show/Get, synchronous, like requesting a web page.
